transcript.text: Thank you all for joining this curriculum review session. As you know, we're considering a classroom pilot of an adaptive writing platform for the fall term. The vendor has offered it at no cost, and the platform can provide individualized writing prompts and feedback to students. Before I approve the proposal, I need your operational findings on several gaps in the draft. Specifically, it doesn't yet specify which grade level will participate, what data settings we'll use, what teacher support will look like, or how we'll orient families. I'd like to hear from each of you in your areas of expertise so we can make informed decisions. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to start by sharing some relevant findings. I actually observed this platform in two seventh-grade classrooms, and what I found is that the useful feedback from the platform depended on a six-week cycle with one coached teacher-planning session each week. I recorded this in my coaching notes, but I realize those notes haven't been attached to the draft proposal. This is directly relevant to the teacher support gap Dr. Shah identified — if we're going to pilot this, we need to build in that weekly coached planning session for the full six-week cycle for the feedback to be genuinely useful for students.

This directly addresses the data settings gap in the draft proposal, and we'll need to build these requirements into our operating plan.
